keyFindings.finding: Three physical MCP registrations exist; two additional paths are symlink aliases.
The provider has standalone launcher and CLI front doors plus shared launcher/worktree integration.
Spec Kit is the primary executable consumer and must update source, exports, tests, and dist atomically.
Four runtime hook families, two OpenCode plugins, a mixed Git hook, and mixed CI depend on the provider.
Eight canonical agents, runtime projections, and at least thirteen command allowlists speak the old contract.
Current doctrine, README, install, doctor, worktree, Skill Advisor, and operator docs require reconciliation.
Historical specs, changelogs, and benchmark reports are immutable inventory, not edit targets.
Removal must be consumer-first, then registration/drain/provider, then shared cleanup/docs/verification.
Ignored DB/process/worktree/user-installed state creates rollback and resurrection risk outside Git.
Unrelated skill, memory, coverage, and council graph subsystems must survive.
